name: Paraguay
snapshot: The collapse of Ueno Bank, owned by a former business partner of President Santiago Peña, led the opposition to file an impeachment motion in November 2026.
culture: Paraguay is the only country in the Americas where most people speak an Indigenous language, Guaraní, which is official alongside Spanish. Tereré, cold yerba mate, is drunk everywhere. The harp and the polka paraguaya are central to its music. The Jesuit missions of the 17th and 18th centuries left UNESCO-listed ruins.
society: Paraguay is a top exporter of soy and beef, and the Itaipú and Yacyretá dams produce more electricity than it uses. Land is very unequally distributed. It is one of the few countries still recognising Taiwan instead of China. Smuggling and money laundering in the tri-border area with Brazil and Argentina are a concern.
situation: Santiago Peña, a former IMF economist, was elected in 2023 with the backing of former president Horacio Cartes, who has been sanctioned by the US for corruption. Peña has aligned closely with Washington, Israel and Argentina's Javier Milei. On 3 November 2026 the central bank seized Ueno Bank, a digital lender with about three million customers that manages about 380 million dollars of state pension money. Ueno belongs to Grupo Vázquez, Peña's business partner until 2025; central bank chief Carlos Carvallo, Ueno's former chair, resigned at Peña's request, and arrest warrants were issued for eight executives. Depositors protested in Asunción, and 35 opposition deputies filed a motion to remove Peña and Vice President Pedro Alliana. It needs 53 of 80 deputies, and the Colorado Party holds majorities in both chambers.
power: A presidential republic. The president is directly elected for a single five-year term; Congress has a Senate and a Chamber of Deputies, both dominated by the Colorado Party.
